title: Agent spec parsing breaks commands that contain colons

finding.claim: Agent spec parsing breaks commands that contain colons
finding.evidence: The parser splits the whole spec with a maximum of two colons, so any command text after a second colon is truncated into the command field and the rest is lost or causes a format error.
finding.recommendation: Parse only the 'agent:' prefix and seat name/options delimiter, leaving the remainder of the string untouched as the command. For example, strip 'agent:' first, split once on the next ':', and treat everything after that as the command verbatim.

refutation.reason: The code explicitly splits on the first colon only (maxsplit=2), then extracts the name from parts[1] and the command from parts[2]. Commands containing colons are preserved intact in parts[2], so the claim that text after a second colon is truncated is false.

probe.summary: `probes/gap_providers_probe.py`, result `gap-providers-cluster.txt`, colon section: - `agent:x:sh -c 'echo a:b'` → name `x`, command `sh -c 'echo a:b'` (the ruling pack's P11 closure case, intact) - `agent:claude:run --flag http://x:8080/a:b` → command `run --flag http://x:8080/a:b` (verbatim, colons and all) - `agent:bot:echo one:two:three:four` → command preserved in full - Options form `agent:my[home=private]:cmd --opt v:1` → name/options parsed, command `cmd --opt v:1` intact
